Where it began

Shan Masood Khan was born in Kuwait City on 14 October 1989. The family soon went back to Karachi, and later moved to England, where he went to Stamford School in Lincolnshire and then Durham University to read economics. He played three first-class games for the university, and later took a distance-learning course in management and sports science at Loughborough.

His first-class debut came in the 2007–08 Quaid-e-Azam Trophy, for Karachi Whites against Hyderabad. He made 54 and shared an opening stand of 154 with Asad Shafiq.

The player

He first played Test cricket against South Africa at the Sheikh Zayed Cricket Stadium in October 2013. He made 75 in the first innings and a duck in the second, and so became only the third Pakistan batter to collect a fifty and a nought on debut. His maiden hundred came at Pallekele in July 2015, when he shared a third-wicket stand of 242 with Younis Khan and Pakistan chased down 382, then their highest successful chase. His best, 156, came against England at Old Trafford in August 2020.

By November 2026 he had played 50 Tests and made 2,926 runs at 30.80, with 7 hundreds and 15 fifties.

Leading the side

He was made Pakistan's Test captain in November 2023 and led them in 16 Tests before stepping down in May 2026. The high point was a home series against England. He made a hundred in the first Test, passing 2,000 Test runs and becoming the 17th Pakistan captain to make a Test century, and Pakistan came from behind to win the next two and take the series 2–1.

Captaincy followed him around. Yorkshire made him their captain for 2023, and he also led Southern Punjab, Multan Sultans, Karachi Kings and Bagh Stallions in the Kashmir Premier League.

What made him special

Given time at the crease, he could bat for a very long while. For Derbyshire in April 2022 he made an unbeaten 201 on the opening day against Sussex, then another double hundred in the very next match, the first Derbyshire batter to do that in first-class cricket.

He also bowled a little medium pace. His first ball in Test cricket, against England at Old Trafford in July 2016, was a no-ball, and his two Test wickets cost 46.00 each, with a best of 1 for 6. It was a hobby, not a second career.

And finally

Kuwait, Karachi, Lincolnshire, Durham, Derbyshire and Yorkshire all came before the Pakistan captaincy. His passport may have been the best-travelled piece of kit in the dressing room.
